name: 409. Passthrough extra params never replace the model, the input or a field the request set (extra-params-guard)
description: With x-bf-passthrough-extra-params: true a caller's extra params are merged into the body sent to the vendor: the extra_params object on the integration routes, every unknown top-level field on the native /v1 routes. The merge used to replace fields the converter had already set. So extra_params.model could send the vendor a model the caller's key does not allow after governance had authorized the model in the request's model field, extra_params.messages or .input could swap the content after the gateway had read it, and a price-affecting field such as size could change what the vendor bills without the unified field showing it (found by the security review of the Voyage provider, and in review of the Tencent provider). The merge is one function, providerUtils.MergeExtraParamsIntoJSON, and it has one rule: an extra param may add a field the request left unset; a request whose extra param names a field the request set, or the model, in any spelling (case and underscores ignored), is refused with 400 caller_invalid_request naming the extra param, before any upstream call. The rule reads the converted body, never a per-provider list. It is pinned in Go for every provider and request type against a local vendor (TestExtraParamsNeverReplaceTheModelOrInputOnAnyProvider, TestExtraParamsModelIsRefusedOnAnOpenAIBasedCustomProvider) and as a table on the merger. These rows pin it on the live wire. On the /openai drop-in routes the planted field sits under extra_params. On the native /v1 routes of an openai-based custom provider it is a second, differently cased top-level key (Model beside model): the gateway reads the request's model from the last of the two, so the planted key comes first and reaches the provider only as an extra param. One row sends a field the request left unset (logprobs on a chat completion) and expects it to arrive. It used dimensions on an embedding until TXE-7059: dimensions is a price-affecting unified field, which an extra param can no longer supply (folder 430).
